question.text: Particle $A$ moves along $X$ -axis with a uniform velocity of magnitude $10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. Particle $B$ moves with uniform velocity $20 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ along a direction making an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the positive direction of $X$ -axis as shown in the figure. The relative velocity of $B$ with respect to that of $A$ is

options.text: $10 \sqrt{5} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ along the bisection of the velocities of A and $B$
